title: Operation Highjump laser-shooting discs

tellings.quote: Admiral Richard Bird Goes Down the coast of Argentina towards Antarctica and he and his Fleet encounter laser shooting discs

Admiral Bird who engaged in Operation High Jump, you know, bringing probably like 70 or so ships, uh, and 33, I think, you know, airplanes and almost 5,000 men down the coast of of Argentina and towards Antarctica. And they reportedly encounter all these flying saucers that are shooting at them with lasers.
tellings.difference: Adds the fleet's size (about 70 ships, 33 aircraft, nearly 5,000 men), credits Forrestal and dates it 1946-1947.
tellings.link_reason: Same Operation Highjump account: Byrd's fleet goes down the coast of Argentina towards Antarctica and meets saucers that shoot lasers.

related.note: Both are about Byrd and Operation Highjump. Dolan reads Byrd's statement as not being about flying saucers, while the story claims the fleet met laser-shooting discs.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells of Operation Highjump, a US Navy expedition led by Admiral Richard Byrd that went down the coast of Argentina toward Antarctica. In one telling Michels describes it as roughly 70 ships, 33 aircraft and almost 5,000 men around 1946 and 1947, and links it to James Forrestal, a top US defence official. According to Michels, the fleet reportedly met flying saucers that shot at them with lasers, which, if true, would mean an early armed clash with unknown craft.
